- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., +1.46, +0.46) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.48, -0.53) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, pushing prices too far from recent mean — especially in 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit recent trends, ignoring longer-term mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early days (1–5) when sentiment is positive, then underestimates later days (15–30) when sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for downward bias.
- If sentiment is positive and price spiked recently, reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid overshoot.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive but recent price is trending down — adjust downward by 1–3%.
- Always check if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average — if yes, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
